paragraphs: This paper studies how to represent uncertainty around data organized into hierarchies. Hyperbolic space is attractive for this purpose because, in theory, trees can be embedded there with arbitrarily little distortion. The hyperbolic wrapped normal distribution brings probabilistic modeling into that space, but the authors show that a commonly used diagonal version has an important geometric mismatch.

The mismatch concerns points at the same level of a hierarchy. In the Poincaré disk representation, the arrangement under study gives these points equal norms and expresses their differences through angular distance. The authors analyze why the diagonal distribution is unsuitable for representing this arrangement. They introduce a rotated version, RoWN, as a simple modification intended to address that problem.

Experiments verify limitations of the original distribution and show that RoWN can alleviate them on a noisy synthetic binary tree, WordNet, and Atari 2600 Breakout. The contribution connects a specific geometric weakness to a targeted distributional change: choosing hyperbolic space alone does not settle how uncertainty should be represented within it.
neurips-2022-a-rotated-hyperbolic-wrappe.tldr: RoWN rotates a hyperbolic probability distribution to alleviate a geometric mismatch in representing hierarchical data.

paragraphs: Stochastic gradient descent usually learns from examples paired with complete target outputs. This paper asks whether obtaining a useful learning update really requires that much supervision. Its starting observation is that stochastic gradients can be accessed without fully supervising every example, opening a different way to think about what information a learning algorithm should request.

The authors formalize this setting as active labeling, an active learning problem involving partial supervision. The focus is on obtaining information that supports gradient updates rather than automatically treating a complete input-output pair as the basic unit of training. They develop a streaming technique and prove that it minimizes the ratio of generalization error to the number of samples in their formulation.

Robust regression provides the paper's detailed illustration of the technique. The significance is the connection between the supervision collected and the updates needed for learning: incomplete target information can still support a principled optimization procedure. The stated guarantee concerns the specified error-to-sample ratio, so its meaning should remain tied to that objective.
neurips-2022-active-labeling-streaming-s.tldr: Active labeling uses partial supervision to obtain stochastic gradients through a streaming method with a guarantee on its error-to-sample ratio.

paragraphs: Evaluating a self-supervised representation commonly requires training a separate prediction head for each downstream task. That consumes computation and task-specific labels. This paper investigates whether the learned features themselves contain a useful signal of representation quality, allowing model selection without repeatedly carrying out those downstream evaluations.

The authors examine the eigenvalues of the empirical feature covariance, which describe how feature variation is distributed across directions. Across the architectures and self-supervised objectives studied, these eigenvalues are well approximated by a power law. Its decay coefficient, alpha, summarizes how quickly their magnitudes fall. Analytical and empirical results identify intervals of alpha associated with excellent generalization for tasks solvable through a linear readout.

Experiments also suggest that design choices in self-supervised algorithms implicitly influence this decay coefficient. For BarlowTwins, using alpha during hyperparameter selection enables a search with less computation. The result offers a feature-based evaluation signal with a clearly stated scope: its quality claims concern downstream tasks that a linear readout can solve.
neurips-2022-alpha-req-assessing-represe.tldr: The decay of feature-covariance eigenvalues provides a task-agnostic quality signal for representations used with linear readouts.

paragraphs: A deployed text model may receive inputs that differ statistically from its training data. Detecting these out-of-distribution inputs matters because unfamiliar samples can lead to model failures. This paper introduces TRUSTED, a detector designed to recognize such departures using information already present in the network's internal representations.

TRUSTED combines two central ideas. First, its detection score uses statistical data depth, a way of assessing how centrally a sample sits within a distribution. Second, it draws on information from all hidden layers of the network. The method therefore treats the network's multiple internal representations as useful evidence for deciding whether an input resembles the training distribution.

The authors evaluate more than 51,000 model configurations, varying checkpoints, random seeds, and datasets. They report state-of-the-art detection performance, with an improvement exceeding three AUROC points. These findings support the usefulness of combining data depth with information across hidden layers for textual detection. The reported gain measures the detector's ability to distinguish distributions; it does not establish that every unfamiliar input will be detected.
neurips-2022-beyond-mahalanobis-distance.tldr: TRUSTED detects unfamiliar text using statistical data depth and information from all hidden layers, improving reported AUROC by over three points.

paragraphs: An explanation method needs a clear target against which its claims can be assessed. This paper frames that target as a causal question: how does changing a real-world concept affect a model's output on actual input data? It introduces CEBaB to make this question concrete for concept-based explanations of language models.

The dataset contains short restaurant reviews and human-written counterfactual versions that modify an aspect of the dining experience, such as food, noise, ambiance, or service. Both the original reviews and their edited counterparts receive sentiment annotations at the aspect and whole-review levels. These ratings undergo multiple validations, giving the benchmark structure beyond an isolated review and a single overall label.

This design supports studying the effects of meaningful concepts rather than only individual input features. The authors use CEBaB to compare explanation methods with different assumptions and interpretations of the explanation problem. They also seek natural metrics for comparing those methods. The contribution is an evaluation setting that links proposed explanations to controlled conceptual changes and observed model behavior.
neurips-2022-cebab-estimating-the-causal.tldr: CEBaB uses human-written counterfactual restaurant reviews to evaluate explanations of how real-world concepts affect NLP model outputs.

paragraphs: Risk scores are sparse linear predictors with integer coefficients, making them compact enough to memorize or print on a small card. Producing accurate scores is harder than this simple format suggests. Rounding logistic regression coefficients does not reliably give high-quality results, while approaches based on mathematical programming can be computationally slow.

FasterRisk first uses beam search to construct a collection of nearly optimal sparse solutions with continuous coefficients. These solutions use different subsets of features, giving the procedure several candidate structures to work with. A second stage turns each candidate into an integer score through a star ray search: it considers different scaling multipliers before rounding coefficients sequentially while seeking to keep logistic loss low.

The algorithm returns the resulting collection of high-quality scores for users to consider, rather than selecting only one feature combination. The authors report that the method finishes within minutes. Its contribution is a practical search procedure that connects accurate continuous solutions to the integer coefficients required by interpretable risk scores while preserving multiple alternatives.
neurips-2022-fasterrisk-fast-and-accurat.tldr: FasterRisk efficiently generates multiple accurate, sparse integer risk scores by combining beam search with scaling and sequential rounding.

paragraphs: Multi-objective integer programs seek solutions under several objectives at once. Objective-space decomposition algorithms tackle them through smaller scalarized problems, but some of those problems can be infeasible or produce nondominated points already found. Such outcomes consume runtime without adding useful solutions. This paper learns a reduction rule intended to reduce that wasted work.

The authors describe the procedure of a generic decomposition algorithm as a Markov decision process. A two-stage graph neural network represents the policy that chooses reductions. Its representation combines information about variables, constraints, and objectives, with particular attention to the objectives. The policy is trained through imitation learning and then inserted into a state-of-the-art decomposition algorithm.

Reported results show a significant improvement in solving efficiency. The learned rule also generalizes fairly well to larger instances and problems with more objectives. The proposed network exceeds existing graph networks for integer programming in test and generalization accuracy. These findings support learning an internal solver decision while retaining the surrounding optimization procedure.
neurips-2022-graph-learning-assisted-mul.tldr: A graph neural network learns reduction decisions that improve the efficiency of a multi-objective integer programming solver.

paragraphs: Standard transformer self-attention builds relationships through pairwise dot products. The authors argue that assuming elements attend directly to one another limits performance on tasks involving higher-order dependencies, including language understanding and image captioning. Jump Self-attention, or JAT, is proposed to let attention represent richer relationships within a transformer.

Inspired by movement in English draughts, JAT applies a spectral convolution technique to the dot-product feature map. This supports propagation within each attention head. The authors also construct higher-order variants under a multi-hop assumption, extending the ways relationships can be represented. JAT is interchangeable with conventional self-attention and compatible with pretrained models, which makes the proposed mechanism usable within existing transformer architectures.

Experiments across ten tasks show significant performance improvements for the proposed methods. The findings support the usefulness of enriching the attention computation beyond direct pairwise relationships in the tested settings. The contribution combines a new attention mechanism with architectural compatibility, connecting the goal of modeling higher-order structure to a component that can replace ordinary self-attention.
neurips-2022-jump-self-attention-capturi.tldr: Jump Self-attention uses spectral convolution and multi-hop relationships to enrich transformer attention, with reported gains across ten tasks.

paragraphs: Adversarial training commonly assigns a perturbed example the same label as its clean source. This paper shows that this practice can introduce label noise: the perturbation distorts the example's true label distribution, while the inherited label ignores that change. The resulting mismatch gives the authors a new perspective on robust overfitting.

Their analysis connects this label noise to the prevalence of robust overfitting and to its dependence on perturbation radius and data quality. The same perspective agrees with their observations of epoch-wise double descent during adversarial training. Together, these connections suggest that the labels used for perturbed examples help explain training behavior that would otherwise appear puzzling.

Guided by that analysis, the authors propose automatically calibrating labels to address both the mismatch and robust overfitting. They report consistent performance improvements across multiple models and datasets without introducing new hyperparameters or extra tuning. The practical contribution is a correction to how adversarial examples are supervised, grounded in an account of why simply inheriting clean labels can be problematic.
neurips-2022-label-noise-in-adversarial-.tldr: Label mismatch in adversarial examples helps explain robust overfitting and motivates automatic label calibration that improves reported performance.

paragraphs: Explanations can reveal more than the reasons behind a neural network's decision. The paper addresses model inversion attacks that reconstruct original images from explanations, potentially exposing sensitive visual information. Its goal is to reduce this leakage while keeping explanations useful for interpreting the model's behavior.

The proposed framework, GNIME, learns to perturb explanations using a noise generator. Training is formulated as a two-player minimax game. An inversion network tries to recover images from explanations, while the generator learns perturbations that interfere with this reconstruction. This makes the defensive changes responsive to the inversion objective, while the framework also seeks to preserve explanation interpretability.

The authors report substantially reduced information leakage while maintaining the original functionality of explanations. In facial recognition models, transferable classification accuracy decreases by up to 84.8%, providing a reported measure of the defense's effect. This is an observed maximum reduction, not a claim of complete privacy. The contribution is a learned approach to balancing explanation usefulness with resistance to reconstruction attacks.
neurips-2022-learning-to-generate-invers.tldr: GNIME learns perturbations that make model explanations harder to invert while preserving their explanatory functionality.

paragraphs: Models with the same architecture and initialization can sometimes combine their capabilities by averaging their parameters. This paper gives that operation a probabilistic interpretation: merged parameters approximately maximize the joint likelihood of the models' parameter posteriors. Under this interpretation, ordinary averaging corresponds to approximating those posteriors with isotropic Gaussian distributions.

Fisher merging replaces that approximation with a Laplace-based Gaussian approximation whose precision matrix is given by Fisher information. Instead of treating parameter uncertainty uniformly, the procedure uses this information to weight the merge. The authors first evaluate the approach in robust fine-tuning and model ensembling, settings where simple parameter averaging is already used, and report improved performance.

They also investigate merging as a way to transfer capabilities between models. In intermediate-task training and domain-adaptive pretraining, Fisher merging is competitive with gradient-based transfer learning while being significantly cheaper. The results establish parameter merging as a distinct route to transfer in those settings. The authors additionally demonstrate combinations of models that had not previously been explored.
neurips-2022-merging-models-with-fisher-.tldr: Fisher merging uses parameter uncertainty to combine compatible models, improving averaging and enabling comparatively inexpensive capability transfer.

paragraphs: Image and text encoders can map their inputs into a shared representation space while still placing the two modalities in separate regions. This paper calls that separation the modality gap and studies it in multimodal models such as CLIP. Its central question is how the gap arises and what consequences its size has.

The authors identify contributions from both initialization and contrastive optimization. They show theoretically and empirically that representations from a common deep network are restricted to a narrow cone at initialization. In a model with two encoders, this produces an initial separation between modalities. Contrastive learning then maintains a distance between them, with the loss function's temperature parameter influencing that distance.

Experiments show that varying the gap can significantly affect improvements in downstream zero-shot classification and fairness. The findings make the geometry of the shared space relevant to more than visualization: separation between modalities has measurable consequences in the tested settings. They also connect those consequences to concrete parts of model construction and training.
neurips-2022-mind-the-gap-understanding-.tldr: Initialization and contrastive learning jointly create a modality gap whose size affects reported zero-shot classification performance and fairness.

paragraphs: Some tasks are awkward to express as a single numerical cost. This paper studies policy optimization with constraints written in linear temporal logic, a language for describing task requirements over time. The framework separates specifying what a policy must accomplish from choosing a policy that performs well according to its cost.

The authors develop a model-based approach that assumes access to a generative model. They reduce the constrained optimization problem to a reachability problem, making it possible to analyze how many samples are needed. Their sample complexity analysis addresses both satisfying the task and achieving cost optimality, rather than evaluating cost alone.

Empirical results show that the algorithm can perform strongly even when samples are limited. The approach matters because it offers a systematic alternative to encoding every task requirement through cost shaping. Its guarantees belong to the stated setting with generative-model access, while the experiments provide evidence that this formal treatment of task requirements can also work well in low-sample regimes.
neurips-2022-policy-optimization-with-li.tldr: Temporal-logic constraints separate task requirements from policy costs, enabling sample guarantees through a reachability-based approach.

paragraphs: Publishing shortest-path distances for every pair of graph vertices while protecting edge weights is difficult. For general graphs, earlier work had roughly linear maximum absolute error in the number of vertices at a fixed privacy budget. This paper breaks that linear barrier with a method that privately releases a constructed synthetic graph.

The construction adds shortcut edges so that every vertex pair has a shortest path using only O(sqrt(n)) links. Noise with a positive mean is then added to edge weights to make the graph differentially private. Standard all-pairs shortest-path computation on the released graph gives O(sqrt(n)) approximation error for fixed privacy parameters. Shortening the number of links in paths is central to the construction.

The authors also study graphs with a small feedback vertex set: a set of vertices whose removal eliminates cycles. If the smallest such set has size k, their specialized algorithm achieves O(k) error. This improves on the general-graph result when k grows more slowly than sqrt(n), making the graph's cycle structure relevant to attainable accuracy.
neurips-2022-private-graph-all-pairwise-.tldr: A private synthetic graph with shortcut edges reduces all-pairs shortest-path approximation error from roughly linear to O(sqrt(n)).

paragraphs: Network pruning compresses an overparameterized model by removing parts of it, often with little loss in overall accuracy. This paper shows that the accuracy effects can be uneven across groups. Pruning may create a disparity that was not present before, or worsen an existing one, even when compression appears attractive from an aggregate perspective.

The authors investigate two factors that may explain this uneven impact: differences between groups in gradient norms and in distance to the decision boundary. These connect group-level outcomes to properties of the model's learning behavior and classification geometry. The paper analyzes both factors in detail and supplies theoretical as well as empirical support for their role.

The authors also propose a simple method that mitigates disparities caused by pruning. The stated result is mitigation rather than elimination of every possible group difference. The contribution broadens how compression quality is assessed: a small overall accuracy change can coexist with meaningful differences in how groups are affected, and those differences can inform the compression procedure.
neurips-2022-pruning-has-a-disparate-imp.tldr: Pruning can unevenly damage group accuracy, and the paper analyzes contributing factors and proposes a mitigation.

paragraphs: A classifier's internal features can contain clues that an input falls outside its training distribution. This paper observes a difference in their singular values: out-of-distribution feature matrices tend to have a larger dominant singular value than in-distribution matrices. It also finds that this dominant component largely determines predictions for unfamiliar samples.

RankFeat turns that observation into a post hoc detection method. It constructs the rank-one matrix associated with the largest singular value and its corresponding singular vectors, then subtracts that matrix from a high-level feature representation. The intervention targets a specific dominant component of the features, directly connecting the proposed method to the observed difference between familiar and unfamiliar inputs.

The authors report state-of-the-art detection performance and a 17.90% reduction in average FPR95 relative to the previous best method. Ablation studies and theoretical analyses support the empirical findings. The result suggests that removing a dominant feature component can help expose distributional differences; the motivating observation is a tendency in the features, not an assertion that every unfamiliar sample has the same structure.
neurips-2022-rankfeat-rank-1-feature-rem.tldr: RankFeat improves out-of-distribution detection by removing the dominant rank-one component of high-level features.

paragraphs: Sliced Wasserstein compares distributions through one-dimensional projections. For images, the conventional procedure first flattens each image into a vector. The authors identify two drawbacks: this does not efficiently capture spatial structure, and every projection direction requires a vector as large as the flattened image, creating a memory burden.

The paper replaces this slicing procedure with methods based on convolution operators. It derives convolution sliced Wasserstein, or CSW, along with variants that incorporate stride, dilation, and nonlinear activation. This brings the slicing operation closer to the spatial organization of image data. The authors investigate metric properties, sample requirements, computational complexity, and connections to conventional sliced Wasserstein distances.

Experiments show favorable performance compared with conventional sliced Wasserstein for comparing image distributions and training deep generative models on images. The contribution is both a new family of image-oriented comparisons and an analysis of their mathematical and computational behavior. The reported findings support convolution as a useful way to construct slices when the samples being compared have image structure.
neurips-2022-revisiting-sliced-wasserste.tldr: Convolution sliced Wasserstein replaces flattened-image projections with convolutional slicing to better accommodate image structure and memory demands.

paragraphs: Federated learning often assumes that participating clients have labeled data. SemiFL addresses a different arrangement: clients have entirely unlabeled data, while the server holds a small labeled dataset. Clients also need to train for multiple local epochs so that they can reduce communication costs instead of repeatedly contacting the server.

The authors analyze data-augmentation-based semi-supervised learning to explain a bottleneck in simply combining it with communication-efficient federated training. Their solution alternates between fine-tuning the global model using labeled data and generating pseudo-labels using that global model. This gives the server's limited supervision an explicit role in the training process used with unlabeled clients.

Extensive experiments show significant performance improvements in the stated setting with a labeled server and clients performing multiple local epochs. SemiFL outperforms many existing semi-supervised federated learning baselines and is competitive with state-of-the-art federated and semi-supervised results. The contribution is a coordinated training procedure for a specific distribution of labels, designed to make use of unlabeled client data while retaining communication efficiency.
neurips-2022-semifl-semi-supervised-fede.tldr: SemiFL alternates server-side labeled training and global-model pseudo-labeling to learn effectively from entirely unlabeled federated clients.

paragraphs: An imitation learner may initially lack information available to its expert. As an episode unfolds, its history of states and actions may reveal the hidden context, eventually allowing it to behave like the expert. This paper studies such asymptotically realizable problems, where the ability to imitate improves as more information becomes available.

The authors prove that on-policy methods are better equipped for this setting, with or without a queryable expert. These methods learn to recover from their own initially suboptimal actions. Off-policy methods instead treat those past actions as though the expert had taken them, which can cause latching: repeatedly choosing earlier actions rather than correcting course as context becomes clearer.

Toy bandit experiments reveal sharp transitions in whether off-policy methods eventually match expert performance, while on-policy methods perform consistently well in that domain. In several continuous-control tasks, on-policy approaches use history to infer context, whereas giving history to off-policy approaches worsens performance. The findings show why access to more history helps only when training handles the learner's own mistakes appropriately.
neurips-2022-sequence-model-imitation-le.tldr: When hidden context becomes identifiable over time, on-policy imitation can learn recovery while off-policy methods may latch onto earlier mistakes.

paragraphs: Embedding-based retrieval ranks candidates using similarities between vectors. Sign random projections compress those vectors into bits, supporting efficient storage, similarity computation, and approximate nearest-neighbor search. This paper proposes SignRFF as an alternative that applies a nonlinear transformation associated with random Fourier features before producing sign-based codes.

Random Fourier features approximate the Gaussian kernel, giving SignRFF a different basis from the cosine-oriented use of sign random projections. The authors develop Ranking Efficiency, an analytical measure for comparing hashing methods. It is closely related to a two-sample mean t-test statistic for binomial variables and provides a common framework for evaluating their ranking behavior.

Under this measure, SignRFF consistently outperforms Gaussian-kernel KLSH and SQ-RFF, and it exceeds SignRP in regions of relatively high similarity. Empirical findings agree with these theoretical comparisons. Further experiments show advantages over a range of data-dependent and deep hashing methods when enough hash bits are available. These qualifications matter: the reported comparisons depend on similarity region, comparator, and, for the broader experiments, sufficient code length.
neurips-2022-signrff-sign-random-fourier.tldr: SignRFF offers a nonlinear binary hashing alternative with favorable ranking analysis and empirical gains under stated similarity and code-length conditions.

paragraphs: This paper examines why a state-value baseline helps on-policy stochastic natural policy gradient optimization. The authors prove that using this baseline allows convergence to a globally optimal policy at an O(1/t) rate. Their analysis provides a convergence result while reconsidering the mechanism usually used to explain the baseline's benefit.

Two findings support the proof. Expected progress satisfies a stochastic version of a non-uniform Łojasiewicz inequality, and the baseline prevents the probability of the optimal action from vanishing with probability one. The latter preserves sufficient exploration. Meanwhile, the variance of natural policy gradient estimates remains unbounded both with and without a baseline, so variance reduction cannot explain the benefit in this setting.

The analysis instead identifies reduced update aggressiveness as the key effect. In the setting studied, controlling that aggressiveness is necessary and sufficient for almost-sure convergence, whereas finite variance is unnecessary. Additional experiments support the theoretical findings. The contribution gives a more specific explanation of how baselines stabilize learning without requiring bounded gradient-estimate variance.
neurips-2022-the-role-of-baselines-in-po.tldr: For the stochastic natural policy gradient setting studied, value baselines enable convergence by controlling update aggressiveness despite unbounded variance.

paragraphs: Distributionally robust optimization interprets learning as protection against adverse changes in the data distribution. This paper connects that viewpoint to Tikhonov regularization. It shows that the regularized objective has an optimal-transport robustness interpretation when an adversary chooses distributions within a suitable neighborhood of the empirical distribution and suitable martingale constraints are imposed.

Those constraints are essential to the stated connection. The paper then relaxes them, creating a broader framework that unifies a class of existing robust methods and yields new regularization tools. This turns the equivalence into a way to design methods: changing the permitted distributional shifts leads to additional forms of regularization within the framework.

The authors propose computational algorithms with provable efficiency to realize the new tools. They also prove a strong duality theorem that could potentially apply to other problems. The contribution links a familiar regularization method to a precisely constrained robustness problem, then uses that link to develop further methods. The possible broader use of the duality theorem remains a prospective application.
neurips-2022-tikhonov-regularization-is-.tldr: Tikhonov regularization admits an optimal-transport robustness interpretation under suitable martingale constraints, whose relaxation yields new regularizers.

paragraphs: Finding an object named in a sentence differs from finding an object suited to an action, such as something to sit comfortably on. TOIST studies the latter problem and extends it from object detection to instance segmentation. Producing object masks gives finer localization, while choosing preferred objects requires comparing several potentially suitable candidates.

The method uses a transformer because attention models relationships between candidate queries. It also introduces noun-pronoun distillation to benefit from pretrained noun-based comprehension models and noun ground truth available during training. Noun prototypes are generated without supervision, and contextual pronoun features learn to select among them. The resulting network remains noun-agnostic when used for inference.

On COCO-Tasks, TOIST reports box mAP 10.7% higher than the best previously reported results. The distillation component adds reported gains of 2.6% in box mAP and 3.6% in mask mAP. These findings support transferring noun-related training information into an action-oriented system that can localize and select useful objects without needing noun information at inference.
neurips-2022-toist-task-oriented-instanc.tldr: TOIST segments objects suited to requested actions, using noun information during training while remaining noun-agnostic at inference.

paragraphs: Radiance field propagation, or RFP, separates a reconstructed 3D scene into individual objects using only unlabeled images from multiple viewpoints. It builds on neural radiance field techniques that jointly represent appearance, geometry, and semantics. The goal is to identify meaningful object regions during reconstruction without annotations, bounding boxes, or prior knowledge of object classes.

The core method propagates individual objects' radiance fields using a bidirectional photometric loss. This enables an unsupervised partition of the scene into object instances. To handle multiple objects and occlusion more effectively, the authors add an iterative expectation-maximization procedure that refines the object masks. The approach therefore combines propagation with repeated refinement of the scene's object assignments.

Experiments produce feasible segmentations that are more accurate than previous unsupervised image or scene segmentation approaches and comparable to existing supervised NeRF-based methods. The resulting separate object representations also enable editing individual 3D objects. These findings demonstrate that multi-view image information can support object separation and reconstruction together without the additional supervision excluded by the method.
neurips-2022-unsupervised-multi-view-obj.tldr: RFP uses unlabeled multi-view images to reconstruct and segment individual 3D objects through radiance-field propagation and mask refinement.

paragraphs: Combinatorial Thompson Sampling chooses combinations of actions while learning their rewards. When finding an exact best combination is difficult, it can rely on an approximation oracle. But this substitution can undermine learning: for some oracles, approximation regret grows linearly with time. This paper asks which oracle properties permit a stronger learning guarantee.

The authors introduce a condition called Reduce2Exact that allows analysis with an approximate oracle to be reduced to exact-oracle analysis. Under that condition, they prove an O(log(T)/Delta) upper bound on approximation regret, where T is the time horizon and Delta is a minimal reward gap. This improves the gap dependence over an earlier O(log(T)/Delta²) bound established for the greedy oracle.

The condition holds in many concrete examples and extends to settings where actions trigger arms probabilistically, including online influence maximization. Its importance is that the guarantee covers an identifiable class of approximation procedures beyond the greedy case. The result remains conditional: it does not claim that an arbitrary approximate oracle makes Thompson Sampling learn effectively.
neurips-2022-when-combinatorial-thompson.tldr: The Reduce2Exact oracle condition yields an O(log(T)/Delta) approximation-regret bound for Combinatorial Thompson Sampling.
